title: Block: 0/1 Knapsack in One Row
oneLiner: Pick items to carry the most value within a weight limit, each item at most once, with a single array filled from the top down.
keyTakeaway: With one array, loop capacity downward for 0/1 knapsack (each item once) and upward for unbounded (items reusable). The loop direction is the entire difference.
explanation:
Item i weighs weights[i] and is worth values[i]. Return the most value you can carry with total weight at most capacity, using each item at most once.

dp[c] is the best value with capacity c using the items seen so far. For each item, go through c from capacity down to the item's weight and set dp[c] = max(dp[c], dp[c - weight] + value): leave the item, or take it on top of the best for the remaining room. Going downward means dp[c - weight] still holds the value from before this item, so it can't be taken twice. Partition Equal Subset Sum and Target Sum are this block; Coin Change is the upward version.

starterCode.python:
def max_value(weights, values, capacity):
    # 1. Make dp of length capacity + 1 filled with 0: dp[c] is the best value with capacity c.
    # 2. For each item, loop the capacity c downward from capacity to the item's weight.
    # 3. Set dp[c] to the larger of dp[c] (skip the item) and dp[c - weight] + value (take it once).
    # 4. Return dp[capacity].
    return 0

gotchas: Looping capacity upward, which lets one item be taken many times.
Stopping the loop at weight + 1 or starting it at capacity - 1, which skips a capacity.

complexity.note: Each of the n items updates up to W capacities once; one array of W + 1 entries is reused for every item.
